AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 5, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION
  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE 54957(b)(1):
  City Manager.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Saji Vargas
  Rock of the Nations Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Daniel Garcia, 5th Grade
  Cresson Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim April as Autism Awareness Month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim April as Fair Housing Month in the City of Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to proclaim April as Counseling Awareness Month in the City of Norwalk.

  IV.  City Council to proclaim March 21, 2022 as World Down Syndrome Day in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Week in Review.

  3.  Recognition of Sergeant Pena and Public Safety Officer Warren for their Outstanding Arrest and Aide to
  a Homeless Individual.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of March
   15, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period February 20, 2022 –
  March 5, 2022, in the total amount of $994,860.14. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  March 10, through March 28, 2022 in the total amount of $6,529,649.80. 640

  Warrant Register

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Herman
  Weissker Power, Inc., Anthony Johnson, and Sharon Woods. 830-08/10/23

  Report

5.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 – CITYWIDE PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT PROGRAM UPDATE
  PHASE 2 - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with Bucknam
  Infrastructure Group, Inc., in the amount of $58,500 to complete Phase 2 of sign inventory and data
  collection; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1045-04

  Report

6.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT - PROJECT MANAGEMENT SUPPORT SERVICES FOR CAPITAL
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS - Staff recommends City Council approve an amendment to the
  agreement with Mario Mera Consultant to continue to provide project management support services in
  a total contract amount not to exceed $60,000 with the option to extend through FY 2022/23; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, and the extension option provided there is
  funding in the Fiscal Year 2022/23 budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 135-07

  Report

7.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT 11522 ALONDRA BOULEVARD - Staff recommends City Council
  confirm the emergency service repair work at 11522 Alondra Boulevard, completed by Stephen Doreck
  Equipment Rentals, Inc., in the amount of $22,068.19. 955

  Report

8.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-19 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME
  HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PLANNING CONTRACT SERVICES – AMENDMENT NO. 4 –
  AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL PLANNING CONSULTANT SERVICES FOR THE
  NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT PROJECT AND ON-CALL BUILDING & SAFETY AND
  PLANNING CONSULTING SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-19, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR
  ADDITIONAL SERVICES FOR THE NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT – CIVIC CENTER
  SPECIFIC PLAN PROJECT, in the amount of $125,000; and

  b.  approve Amendment No. 4 to the agreement with Infrastructure Engineers to provide on-call
  professional building and planning consultant services in an amount not-to-exceed $150,000 and
  Additional Services in an amount not to exceed $125,000 through November 2022 for a total of
  $275,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment and any additional
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, provided there is funding in the budget, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 135-07/610/810-09

  Report
   9.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 - ONLINE APPLICATION TOOLS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with CampaignRep for online application tools not to
  exceed $26,600; and authorize the City Manager to execute this amendment, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 145-06

  Report

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 22-20 - OPPOSITION TO INITIATIVE 21-0042A – TAXPAYER PROTECTION AND
  GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY ACT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-20,
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK OPPOSING INITIATIVE 21-
  0042A - TAXPAYER PROTECTION AND GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY ACT.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 31, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
